rationale: C15 plausibly supplied a material drafting template. Both are letters from Eisenhower to Bulganin that answer Soviet proposals through the same recurring sequence: assess proposals for reducing tension and armaments; insist on international supervision and aerial inspection; direct further work to United Nations disarmament machinery; promise continued study or new proposals; and close by reaffirming pursuit of peace. The child contains language and organization close enough to C15 to exceed shared-topic similarity. C12 and C25 contain substantial related material, but C15 is the closest antecedent in structure, addressee, and formulation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I have given careful consideration to the declaration by the Soviet Government... but find myself in basic disagreement with the analysis of your government as it relates to the source of international tension.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I refer to your letter of June 6 to which I have given a great deal of thought... However, I doubt that such reductions... will contribute effectively to eliminate the fear... generated by national armaments.
shared_material.explanation: Both open by acknowledging and carefully considering Bulganin's communication, then immediately qualify or reject its analysis while retaining a diplomatic tone.

shared_material.child_excerpt: your government's declaration does not signify willingness to seek agreement on the basic element of my Geneva proposal of averting surprise attack through aerial inspection of the centers of our military power.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: So far, I understand that you reject this... What I proposed was... designed to make known to each other that neither of us is preparing a sudden massive attack against the other.
shared_material.explanation: This is the same distinctive Geneva aerial-inspection machinery, presented as a safeguard against surprise attack and adapted to the new Soviet declaration.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The United States is giving this and your other disarmament proposals careful study. We are prepared to discuss them... in forthcoming meetings of the Disarmament Subcommittee.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I and my associates have never ceased to give the most intensive study to this whole matter... Discussions [in the United Nations Disarmament Subcommittee] have done much to shed light on this difficult problem.
shared_material.explanation: Both couple continued executive study with further negotiation through the same United Nations Disarmament Subcommittee.

shared_material.child_excerpt: our government will continue its efforts in behalf of effective control and reduction of all armaments... seek a stable foundation for a just and durable peace
shared_material.parent_excerpt: it is my earnest hope that we will find ways to make progress toward a meaningful control of armaments... fruitful of good for all the world
shared_material.explanation: The child preserves C15's closing movement from controlled armament reduction to an affirmative statement of enduring peaceful purpose.
